stories.title: Northwind Provides $231M Construction Loan to Convert 675 Third Avenue
stories.excerpt: David Werner Real Estate Investments and Nathan Berman’s MetroLoft have secured $231 million in construction financing to convert an office at 675 Third Avenue into a 450-unit residential multifamily in Midtown Manhattan, Commercial Observer can first report. Ran Eliasaf’s Northwind Group provided the construction debt, which will refinance existing acquisition debt on the asset and fund a build-out that has already begun. No broker was listed on the transaction. Northwind had previously provided a $90 million acquisition loan to sponsorship, who purchased the property from the Durst Organization in April 2025 for $100 million. Eliasaf told Commercial Observer that his firm felt “very comfortable” with the building’s layout and the experienced sponsorship group, which is led by Berman, one of the preeminent experts of office-to-residential conversions in New York City. “It’s a fairly simple conversion, with no structural work,” said Eliasaf. “It’s basically an interior fit-out, and it’s technically [an asset] that spans the full block of Third Avenue from 42 Street to 43 Street near Grand Central Terminal. Eliasaf added that sponsorship had already started construction financed by equity and that his firm “came in with capital to take it to the next level.” A full 25 percent of the rental units in the property will be designated as affordable housing under the 467-m program, according to Northwind. The construction loan from Northwind comes only a few months after MetroLoft and David Werner oversaw an alarming structural collapse in early July at the former Pfizer headquarters at 235 East 42nd Street and 219 East 42nd Street, which is being converted into a 1,600-unit apartment building, with 11 floors being added to the existing structure. CO reported that collapsing columns and falling bricks inside the property on July 7 led to evacuations in neighboring buildings and street closures. Workers managed to stabilize the shifting building by the following morning. El
bullets: Northwind Group closes $231M construction loan, Midtown Manhattan office-to-residential conversion
675 Third Avenue: 450 units, acquisition price $100M (April 2025), minimal structural work required
MetroLoft/Nathan Berman leading sponsor; lender cites simple interior fit-out, experienced team confidence
stories.summary: Northwind Group provided $231 million in construction financing for the conversion of 675 Third Avenue in Midtown Manhattan into a 450-unit residential property, refinancing a prior $90 million acquisition loan. The sponsorship group, led by MetroLoft's Nathan Berman, purchased the office building from Durst for $100 million in April 2025. The conversion requires minimal structural work—essentially an interior fit-out—and construction has already begun.
stories.impact: Office-to-residential conversions in Manhattan remain fundable and attractive to institutional lenders, signaling continued capital availability for repositioning aging Manhattan office stock into housing. This accelerates de-risking of the Midtown office sector while adding to multifamily supply in a supply-constrained, high-demand submarket. Watch for similar conversion greenlight volumes as a bellwether of capital conviction in office-to-resi arbitrage across NYC submarkets.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Exclusively Lists 54 Acres Near Michigan Nuclear Power Plant
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap announced the exclusive listing of 53.54 acres near the Enrico Fermi Nuclear Power Plant and existing high-voltage transmission infrastructure in southeast Michigan. “The property’s proximity to established electrical infrastructure and major transportation routes makes it an opportunity worth evaluating for developers and investors with significant power requirements,” said Joseph Carrizales, associate of investments in Marcus & Millichap’s Detroit office. “The offering allows buyers to assess the site’s potential based on their specific development needs and investment criteria.” Carrizales has the exclusive listing to market the property on behalf of a private ownership group. Located on Leroux Road in Frenchtown Charter Township, the property is approximately 35 yards from an ITC high-voltage transmission line and 505 yards from an ITC transmission substation. The site also offers access to Interstate 75 and North Dixie Highway, positioning it for consideration by developers and investors evaluating land for energy-intensive uses. The property is zoned for agricultural use, and any alternative development would require applicable approvals. bullets: 54 acres near Enrico Fermi Nuclear Plant, southeast Michigan, marketed via Marcus & Millichap

Positioning for energy-intensive development; requires zoning/entitlement approvals
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap has listed 53.54 acres in Frenchtown Charter Township near the Enrico Fermi Nuclear Power Plant and high-voltage transmission infrastructure in southeast Michigan. The site is approximately 35 yards from an ITC transmission line and 505 yards from a transmission substation, with access to I-75 and North Dixie Highway. Currently zoned agricultural; any alternative development requires municipal approval.
stories.impact: Low relevance to multifamily development. This is land marketed for energy-intensive industrial/data center uses (power generation, cryptomining, manufacturing) rather than residential. However, data center and industrial clusters can indirectly drive population and worker migration that supports multifamily demand in nearby communities—monitor if this site catalyzes broader southeast Michigan economic activation.

stories.title: BridgeCity Lends $28M for Williamsburg Multifamily Development
stories.excerpt: Domes Properties has secured $28 million of acquisition and construction financing to develop a multifamily project in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. BridgeCity Capital provided the loan for Domes’ planned 45-unit apartment building at 87 Havemeyer Street. Domes Properties, through the entity 87 Havemeyer Street LLC, acquired the three-parcel development site for $13 million from Michael Pescatore, PincusCo. previously reported. EJ Ehrlich, director of originations at BridgeCity Capital, said the loan marks the start of a new lending relationship with Domes, which he described as “an accomplished sponsor recognized for their development expertise and exceptional track record of execution.” Domes Properties is a division of Brooklyn-based Domes Management. Meridian Capital Group negotiated the transaction. The Michael Krariem-designed project will rise seven stories and 47,000 gross square feet. Resident amenities will include a fitness center, coworking space, a rooftop lounge, and an outdoor terrace. Domes Properties did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BridgeCity Capital closes $28M acquisition/construction loan, Williamsburg, Brooklyn
Domes Properties: 45 units at 87 Havemeyer Street, $13M land acquisition, 7-story build
Developer track record strong; amenities include fitness, coworking, rooftop lounge; 47K GSF
stories.summary: Domes Properties secured $28 million in acquisition and construction financing from BridgeCity Capital for a 45-unit multifamily development at 87 Havemeyer Street in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. The sponsor acquired the three-parcel site for $13 million and will build a seven-story, 47,000-square-foot building with market-rate units and amenities including fitness center, coworking space, and rooftop lounge.
stories.impact: Smaller-scale ground-up development in Williamsburg remains financeable despite higher interest rate environment, suggesting lender appetite for experienced sponsors and tight value-add plays in supply-constrained Brooklyn neighborhoods. Track Williamsburg's absorption rates and rent growth to gauge whether 40–60 unit projects can compete for capital as larger-scale developments push costs higher.

stories.title: MBTA Issues RFQ for Redevelopment of Lynn Commuter Parking Garage
stories.excerpt: The Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority (MBTA) has issued a request for qualifications from would-be redevelopers of its downtown Lynn, MA commuter parking garage. It’s the first of a two-step process, to be followed by a request for proposals. The five-story garage opened in 1992 and has been partially closed since 2022 over safety concerns, ItemLive reported. Of its 948 parking spaces, approximately 350 are currently available. In December 2024, the City of Lynn and MBTA unveiled an initial concept that called for retaining part of the garage for parking while demolishing the remainder to make way for transit-oriented development. The city’s priorities for the property include a mix of residential, commercial, and transit uses, along with businesses and amenities to serve residents, workers, and visitors. MBTA’s RFQ also calls for inclusionary zoning requiring 10% of housing units to be affordable to households earning 60% of the area median income. Photo courtesy of MBTA. The post MBTA Issues RFQ for Redevelopment of Lynn Commuter Parking Garage appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MBTA Lynn parking garage: 948 spaces, 350 currently available, partially closed since 2022
RFQ issued for mixed-use redevelopment (residential, commercial, transit); 10% affordable housing required
City/transit authority concept: retain partial parking, demolish remainder for TOD
stories.summary: The Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority issued a request for qualifications to redevelop its five-story parking garage in downtown Lynn, MA. Built in 1992 with 948 spaces, the structure has been partially closed since 2022 due to safety concerns, leaving approximately 350 spaces available. The concept calls for retaining some parking while demolishing the remainder for mixed-use, transit-oriented development with 10% affordable housing requirement.
stories.impact: Transit-oriented redevelopment opportunity in Lynn signals demand for infill multifamily near MBTA stations; 10% affordability mandate will compress returns but aligns with Massachusetts housing policy. Monitor site disposition and feasibility studies—Lynn's proximity to Boston and transit access make this an attractive potential multifamily development anchor, though affordability requirements will tighten underwriting. Early mover advantage for developers with government relations and mixed-income expertise in Greater Boston.

stories.title: Kidder Mathews Arranges Sale of 45-Unit Multifamily in Walla Walla
stories.excerpt: Suncrest Apartments, a 45-unit multifamily community located at 1800 Evergreen Street in Walla Walla, Washington, has sold for $4.3 million. Kidder Mathews Vice President Max Frame of the Simon | Anderson Multifamily Team in Seattle represented the seller, Art Griff, in the transaction. The buyer was Jason Zook. Situated on 1.72 acres, Suncrest Apartments consists primarily of two-bedroom units and offers investors a value-add opportunity. The sale represents the property’s first change of ownership in 45 years, with Kidder Mathews serving as the sole brokerage firm involved. “Properties that have been held by the same owner for nearly half a century don’t come to market often,” said Frame. “Suncrest offered a rare opportunity to acquire an established apartment community with significant value-add potential. The size of the transaction also speaks to the investment opportunities we’re seeing in markets outside Washington’s major metropolitan areas.” The post Kidder Mathews Arranges Sale of 45-Unit Multifamily in Walla Walla appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Suncrest Apartments, Walla Walla, WA: 45 units sell for $4.3M after 45-year hold
1.72 acres, primarily 2-bed units; first ownership change in 45 years; value-add opportunity
Kidder Mathews transaction signals investor appetite for secondary-market multifamily assets
stories.summary: Suncrest Apartments, a 45-unit multifamily property at 1800 Evergreen Street in Walla Walla, Washington, sold for $4.3 million to investor Jason Zook. The property, held by original owner Art Griff for 45 years, sits on 1.72 acres and consists primarily of two-bedroom units. The transaction represents a rare change of ownership and was marketed as a value-add opportunity.
stories.impact: Generational ownership transitions in secondary markets like Walla Walla are creating entry points for value-add investors. The $4.3M price on 45 units (~$96K per unit) reflects lower cost structure than West Coast metros, but limited narrative on Walla Walla's job growth, population trends, or rent trajectory. Monitor Washington State smaller markets for similar portfolio turnover; these sales suggest investor appetite for operator-focused value-add in non-major metros, potentially signaling capital deployment outside Seattle/Portland.

stories.title: Goldman Sachs Provides $43M Refi for Long Island Office Complex
stories.excerpt: Capstone Equities has secured $43 million to finance Franklin Avenue Plaza, a four-building, 488,835-square-foot office complex in Long Island, N.Y., Commercial Observer can first report. Goldman Sachs provided the debt as part of a larger commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) securitization, which replaced a loan from Argentic that Capstone used to acquire the property in 2025. Newmark‘s Daniel Fromm, Ryan Bub, and Stavros Giannakopoulos arranged the transaction. Located at 1205–1325 Franklin Avenue in Garden City, a Long Island suburb 20 miles east of Manhattan, Franklin Avenue Plaza encompasses four buildings, each no more than five stories, that opened around 1979. Capstone Equities did not respond to requests for comment. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialoberver.com.
bullets: Goldman Sachs closes $43M CMBS refi for Long Island office complex via securitization
Franklin Avenue Plaza: 488.8K SF, 4 buildings, Garden City (20 miles east of Manhattan), built ~1979
Capstone Equities replaced 2025 Argentic acquisition loan; debt part of larger CMBS securitization
stories.summary: Capstone Equities refinanced Franklin Avenue Plaza, a four-building, 488,835-square-foot office complex in Garden City, Long Island, with a $43 million loan from Goldman Sachs as part of a CMBS securitization. The property, located at 1205–1325 Franklin Avenue approximately 20 miles east of Manhattan, consists of buildings opened around 1979, each five stories or fewer. The refinance replaced acquisition debt Capstone used to purchase the property in 2025.
stories.impact: Low direct relevance to multifamily development. However, CMBS appetite for Long Island office assets—despite structural office headwinds—suggests capital markets remain selective but open for seasoned, stabilized properties with strong tenant bases. This signals that office-to-residential conversion financing will remain available for similar-vintage, well-located Long Island assets if sponsors pursue residential conversion on adjacent land or nearby parcels. Watch for follow-on conversion RFPs in Long Island's Garden City submarket.

stories.title: MacKenzie Management Secures 310K SF in Maryland Assignments
stories.excerpt: MacKenzie Management Company has secured five new assignments to provide comprehensive property management and maintenance services for approximately 310,000 square feet of commercial office, medical condominium, retail, and warehouse/industrial space across the Maryland region. The assets are 901 Ostend Street and 1212 65th Street in Baltimore City; 7257 Parkway Drive in Anne Arundel County; 111 Bata Boulevard in Harford County; and 5708 Frederick Avenue in Montgomery County. MacKenzie Management Property Managers Alex Bartlett, Kati Coles, Kevin Kimmel, and Marie Gerwig will oversee all day-to-day activities for these assignments. With the assignments, MacKenzie Management Company now provides property management services to more than 200 properties totaling approximately 10 million square feet across all asset classes. “We have built a critical mass of assets, which has provided us with increased buying power and the ability to reduce costs, which we pass on to the buildings we manage,” said Jill Harman, President of MacKenzie Management. The post MacKenzie Management Secures 310K SF in Maryland Assignments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MacKenzie Management secures 5 new property management assignments across Maryland
~310K SF commercial office, medical, retail, industrial across Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Harford, Montgomery
MacKenzie now manages 200+ properties totaling ~10M SF; expanded scale driving cost efficiencies
stories.summary: MacKenzie Management Company secured five new property management assignments totaling approximately 310,000 square feet of office, medical, retail, and industrial space across Maryland. The assets span Baltimore City (two properties), Anne Arundel, Harford, and Montgomery counties. With these additions, MacKenzie now manages over 200 properties totaling approximately 10 million square feet across all asset classes.
stories.impact: Low relevance to multifamily development. Property management scale announcements are operational rather than demand/supply signals. However, MacKenzie's purchasing power gains and cost-reduction benefits suggest regional management consolidation in Mid-Atlantic markets, which may improve operational margins for institutional multifamily owners in Maryland/Baltimore. Monitor if MacKenzie expands into multifamily PM, which could signal developer interest in outsourced operations for mid-size portfolios.

stories.title: Benefit Street Partners Provides $48M Refi for Brooklyn Mixed-Income Multifamily
stories.excerpt: The Hudson Companies has secured $47.6 million to refinance the Clark, a 170-unit, mixed-income multifamily property in Brooklyn, Commercial Observer can first report. Benefit Street Partners provided the debt, while Newmark’s Daniel Fromm, Samuel Speciale and Lance Tillman arranged the financing. Chris Zedano, managing director at the Hudson Companies, noted in a statement that the new debt is expected to place his asset, which opened in 2018 with tax benefits, “on strong, stable footing” and create an enduring housing option in Brooklyn’s Prospect Lefferts Gardens neighborhood. The Hudson Companies used the now-expired 421-a affordable housing abatement to finance construction of the property. “We built the Clark with the goal of delivering high-quality, mixed-income housing to Prospect Lefferts Gardens, and that commitment hasn’t changed,” added Zendano. Located at 310 Clarkson Avenue in Brooklyn, the Clark stands eight stories and includes market-rate, rent-stabilized and affordable housing units. The asset also features 7,700 square feet of ground-floor retail space. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Benefit Street Partners closes $47.6M refi for Hudson Companies' mixed-income multifamily, Brooklyn
The Clark: 170 units, Prospect Lefferts Gardens, 8-story, 421-a tax abatement expired
Asset opened 2018; mix of market-rate, rent-stabilized, affordable units; 7.7K SF ground-floor retail
stories.summary: Hudson Companies refinanced the Clark, a 170-unit mixed-income multifamily property in Brooklyn's Prospect Lefferts Gardens, with $47.6 million in debt from Benefit Street Partners. The property, located at 310 Clarkson Avenue, opened in 2018 using the now-expired 421-a affordable housing tax abatement. It includes market-rate, rent-stabilized, and affordable units plus 7,700 square feet of ground-floor retail.
stories.impact: Expiring 421-a abatement signals refinancing urgency as stabilized New York affordable mixed-income properties lose tax benefits. Benefit Street Partners' willingness to finance implies strong cash flow and mission-aligned capital appetite for permanently affordable housing. Developers should expect refinance windows for 2018–2020 421-a projects to close over next 12–18 months; opportunity for acquisition of stabilized assets at reduced basis as sellers seek liquidity before abatement cliff. Prospect Lefferts Gardens rents and submarket fundamentals will drive forward underwriting.

stories.title: Brightshore Acquires Newly Built Long Island City Luxury Apartments
stories.excerpt: Brightshore Capital LP, formerly GTIS Partners, has acquired DŌMI, a newly constructed, 190-unit luxury multifamily property located at 29-24 40th Ave. in Long Island City, for slightly more than $143 million. The acquisition through Brightshore’s Opportunity Zone Fund II was financed with a $98.5-million loan from Affinius Capital. The seller was a joint venture of SB Development, Hazelton Capital Group and Avenue Realty Capital. “Long Island City has benefited from sustained residential expansion, fueled by convenient access to Manhattan, robust transportation links and continued investment in local infrastructure and neighborhood amenities,” said Rob Vahradian, partner at Brightshore. “We believe the combination of these fundamentals and the limited availability of new residential development opportunities create an attractive environment for long-term investment.” The Newmark Investment Sales Team of Eric Roth, Daniel O’Brien, Adam Spies and Adam Doneger arranged the sale. Jordan Roeschlaub, Christopher Kramer and Max Ralby of the Newmark Debt & Structured Finance Team arranged the loan from Affinius. The post Brightshore Acquires Newly Built Long Island City Luxury Apartments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Brightshore Capital acquires DŌMI, Long Island City luxury apartments, for $143M+
190 units, newly constructed, 29-24 40th Ave; $98.5M Affinius Capital loan; Opportunity Zone Fund II
Sellers: SB Development, Hazelton Capital, Avenue Realty; strong infrastructure/transportation drivers cited
stories.summary: Brightshore Capital LP acquired DŌMI, a newly constructed 190-unit luxury multifamily property at 29-24 40th Ave in Long Island City, for slightly more than $143 million. The purchase was financed with a $98.5 million loan from Affinius Capital through Brightshore's Opportunity Zone Fund II. The seller was a joint venture of SB Development, Hazelton Capital Group, and Avenue Realty Capital.
stories.impact: Stabilized, recently-delivered luxury product in Long Island City remains acquisition-attractive to opportunity zone capital; $143M for 190 units (~$753K/unit) reflects tight supply and sustained demand in waterfront LIC submarket. Early-stage developer/sponsor exits at strong valuations signal confidence in LIC fundamentals. This reinforces LIC as a preferred destination for capital relative to other Queens submarkets. Monitor 2025 delivery pipeline in LIC for absorption rates; limited new supply window may support rent growth and justify continued investor acquisitions of existing product.

stories.title: Nuveen Acquires $445M Retail Portfolio Across Three Western States
stories.excerpt: Nuveen Real Estate has acquired a 13-property retail portfolio in California, Colorado and Washington for $445.5 million in what is likely one of the largest grocery-anchored shopping center transactions in the Western U.S. in recent years. The portfolio is 93.5 percent leased. It includes 1.89 million square feet of open-air retail space, with six properties in California, four in Colorado and three in Washington, according to an announcement Monday from JLL, which represented Nuveen in the acquisition. The deal values the portfolio at approximately $236 per square foot. The portfolio’s California assets are Santa Susana Plaza in Simi Valley; Marin Gateway in Sausalito; Marketplace at Birdcage in Citrus Heights; Santa Rita Plaza in Salinas; TJ Maxx Plaza in Roseville; and Tracy Pavilion in Tracy. Major tenants include Safeway, Walmart Neighborhood Market, Sprouts, FoodMaxx and Grocery Outlet. Other national retailers include Target, TJ Maxx, Marshalls, Ross and Best Buy. U.S. Bank provided $239 million in financing for 11 of the 13 properties. The debt covers 54 percent of the portfolio’s total purchase price. JLL did not disclose the interest or maturity date. “Investor demand for high-quality, well-located retail remains strong, and this portfolio provides Nuveen with scale and geographic diversification across multiple West Coast markets,” JLL Managing Director Daniel Tyner said in a statement. “The combination of well-located infill centers paired with future growth potential at each asset made this portfolio extremely attractive in today’s market.” JLL added that limited new construction in the three states paired with significant residential populations have supported demand for grocery-anchored shopping centers. The deal also comes as institutional investors increasingly target grocery-anchored and other open-air retail properties due to tenant demand and limited supply. JLL’s team included Tyner, Geoff Tranchina, Gleb Lvovich and Eric Kathrein.
bullets: Nuveen acquires 13-property retail portfolio, CA/CO/WA, for $445.5M; 93.5% leased
1.89M SF grocery-anchored open-air centers; 6 CA, 4 CO, 3 WA locations; $236/SF valuation
Major tenants: Safeway, Walmart; largest grocery-anchored shopping center deal in Western US in years
stories.summary: Nuveen Real Estate acquired a 13-property, grocery-anchored retail portfolio across California, Colorado, and Washington for $445.5 million. The portfolio consists of 1.89 million square feet of open-air retail space across six California properties (Simi Valley, Sausalito, Citrus Heights, Salinas, Roseville, Tracy), four Colorado properties (Littleton, Aurora, Englewood areas), and three Washington properties (Port Orchard, Lake Stevens, Des Moines). Portfolio is 93.5 percent leased and valued at approximately $236 per square foot.
stories.impact: Low direct relevance to multifamily development. However, Nuveen's significant capital deployment into grocery-anchored retail in Western secondary markets reflects confidence in these submarkets' residential stability and spending power. This signals continued population/household formation in non-major metros across California, Colorado, and Washington—underscoring hidden demand in 'secondary' West Coast submarkets that multifamily developers should assess for ground-up or conversion opportunities. Monitor Nuveen portfolio occupancy trends; sustained >90% retail occupancy suggests healthy residential fundamentals in these markets.
